: Press with your thumb on the muscle beside the shin crest, 4 finger widths (approx. 3 cun) below the kneecap (ST36), then in the hollow under the inner edge of the bone, below the knee (SP9); do not press on the bone; use steady pressure.
: Compare the two calves: if they differ (one more swollen, warmer, red or painful), stop the sequence.

: With your thumbs, press lightly, one after the other, on the inner wrist: in the hollow on the little-finger side (HT7), then at the middle, 3 finger widths (approx. 2 cun) above the crease (PC6), holding steady.
: If both calves look the same, knead the calf between your palms, without pressing directly behind the knee.
I have heart disease, an arrhythmia or hard-to-control high blood pressure
I have kidney disease or kidney stones
I have epilepsy or have had seizures
I have glaucoma, a fragile retina or recent eye surgery
I have an abdominal or inguinal hernia, an aortic aneurysm, fluid in the abdomen, a stoma or recent abdominal surgery
I have lymphedema or have had lymph nodes removed (armpit/groin), or I have a dialysis fistula or a catheter in one arm
I have or have had cancer, including with bone involvement, or I am undergoing cancer treatment
Dizziness in the morning, unstable blood pressure, fever. Be gentle and avoid intense pressure. In pregnancy, skip LI4 (step 6) and ask your doctor for approval.

Place the pad of your thumb on the point and increase the pressure gradually, over 3–5 seconds, to a comfortable pressure (4–6 out of 10), never painful. Hold steady, breathing slowly, then release slowly. Do not repeat more than 2–3 times on the same point in one session.

With two fingers of one hand, apply light pressure on CV12, at the midpoint of the line between the lower sternum and the navel. At the same time, with one finger of the other hand, press gently on ST25, 3 finger widths (approx. 2 cun) to the side of the navel. Breathe slowly into your belly for 45–60 seconds, then do the other side.
With lymphedema, after lymph node removal or after radiotherapy to the area, do not massage the limb without your doctor's approval.

With the opposite hand, grasp the wrist: thumb on PC6, between the two tendons, 3 finger widths (approx. 2 cun) above the wrist crease, and the tip of the index or middle finger on HT7, in the crease, on the little-finger side. Press simultaneously, light to medium (3–5/10), for 60 seconds, with slow breaths; stop if you feel tingling, numbness or an electric-shock sensation in the fingers; switch hands.

With one hand, place your thumb on ST36, 4 finger widths (approx. 3 cun) below the kneecap, lateral to the edge of the tibia, and with the other, place your thumb on SP6, 4 finger widths (approx. 3 cun) above the ankle, on the posterior edge of the tibia. Press simultaneously, with medium, comfortable pressure (4–6/10), for 60–90 seconds.
With a pacemaker or other implanted device, do not press over the device area (below the collarbone, sternum); ask your doctor.
With reduced sensation in the foot, do not do this exercise; ask your doctor or podiatrist for a safe routine (daily inspection of the soles is more important than massage).
If you are pregnant, take anticoagulants, have a pacemaker, osteoporosis, cancer or circulation problems in the legs, complete it before the first session (it takes a minute).
If you take anticoagulants or have a clotting disorder: light pressure only (maximum 3 out of 10), no ball or forearm, 20–30 s per point; stop if bruising appears. Ask your doctor.

If you take anticoagulants, antiplatelet drugs or have clotting disorders, ask your doctor what intensity is acceptable; until then, light pressure only (maximum 3 out of 10), no ball or forearm, 20–30 s per point.
If none of these signs match and the pain persists beyond 48 hours, see a doctor.
Relaxation of the facial muscles and a feeling of facial relaxation; it does not treat sinusitis.
Difficulty breathing, chest pain or pressure, sudden weakness on one side, slurred speech or fainting: stop immediately and call 112.
Severe abdominal pain, high fever, a swollen, warm and painful calf or arm on one side only: do not massage and go to the emergency room.

New, severe or worsening abdominal pain, with fever, vomiting, a hard abdomen or blood in the stool: do not massage, go to the emergency room. In pregnancy, any abdominal pain or bleeding requires immediate evaluation.
Severe or worsening abdominal pain, repeated vomiting or vomiting blood, blood in the stool; in pregnancy, any bleeding or abdominal pain
Sudden, intense or unexplained pain, or a recent injury or fall in the area to be massaged

Pain radiating down the arm, numbness, dizziness, recent neck injury or acute cervical disc herniation. Do not press on the side of the neck and do not force movements. In pregnancy, ask your doctor for approval and skip GB21 (step 2).

Pain radiating down the leg, weakness or numbness, fever, recent injury, lumbar surgery; not over the kidneys and not directly on the spine. Keep the ball on muscle only; if sharp pain appears, take your weight off the ball. In pregnancy, do not do this sequence (the lumbosacral area and buttocks are to be avoided: BL25, BL26, BL32, GB30), unless your doctor approves.
Sudden headache, like a blow, “the worst of your life”, or headache with fever and a stiff neck, vomiting or confusion

New headache, appearing suddenly or after age 50, with tenderness at the temples or scalp, pain when chewing or vision disturbances: seek medical evaluation the same day; if it is “the worst of your life”, call 112.
Neck pain with fever and stiffness, after an injury or with weakness in one arm: an emergency, not acupressure.
Back or leg pain with numbness in the area between the legs, weakness in both legs, or new problems with urination or bowel movements
Low back pain with numbness between the legs, weakness in one or both legs, or new problems with urination or bowel movements: call 112 or go immediately to the emergency room.
New pain or cramp in one calf, with swelling, warmth or redness on one side only: do not massage the leg and go to the emergency room the same day.
Chest pain or tightness, shortness of breath, fainting or unusual palpitations
Chest pain, shortness of breath, sudden weakness on one side of the body, slurred speech or a headache like a blow: call 112 immediately.
Pain between the shoulder blades or in the chest, with shortness of breath, sweating or radiation to the arm/jaw: call 112.

Severe pains, numbness in the arms, dizziness, recent neck injury, acute cervical disc herniation; no pressure on the side of the neck. Agree on a stop signal (the word “stop” or a raised hand) before you start; the person giving the massage asks every 1–2 minutes “how is the pressure?” (target: 4–6 out of 10), and the recipient can ask at any time for lighter, firmer or stopping, without explanations. On request, or at sharp pain, numbness or dizziness, you stop immediately. In pregnancy, skip GB21 (step 2) and ask your doctor for approval. Pressure goes on the muscle, not deep, without tilting the head back. If dizziness, double vision, slurred speech, difficulty swallowing, weakness in one arm or new, intense pain in the neck appears, stop and call 112.
